q: Rate is a measure of how fast or how slow the ____ is.
e: Reaction rate quantifies the speed at which reactants are converted into products.

q: To describe the quantitative measurement of a reaction rate, it is necessary to specify how fast the reactants are used up or the ____ are formed.
e: Rates can be measured by tracking the disappearance of reactants or the appearance of products over time.

q: The rate of reaction means measuring the change in the amount of a product produced or a reactant used up in the ____ taken for that change.
e: Time is the fundamental variable in the denominator of any reaction rate expression.

q: The reaction rate is usually expressed as the change in the amount of a reactant used up or the product formed in a unit of ____.
e: Rate is always expressed as a change in quantity per unit time.

q: If the substance is a gas, the amount consumed or formed is expressed in pressure units or as measured in ____.
e: Gaseous reactants or products can be monitored by measuring changes in their volume or pressure.

q: ____ units are used if the reactant or product is in solution.
e: For reactions in solution, molar concentration is the standard unit for measuring the amount of substance.

q: Generally, in chemical reactions, the rate of a reaction in solution is measured in terms of a decrease in the concentration of the reactant or an increase in the concentration of the product per unit time at a constant ____.
e: Temperature must be kept constant when measuring reaction rates because it significantly affects the rate.

q: In the rate equation, the delta ($\Delta$) means ____.
e: The delta symbol represents the difference between final and initial values of a quantity.

q: In the rate equation, the square bracket [] represents molar ____.
e: Square brackets are the standard chemical notation for expressing molar concentration (mol/dm³).

q: The minus (-) sign means a ____ in the concentration of the reactant.
e: Reactants are consumed during a reaction, so their change in concentration is negative, requiring a minus sign to make the rate positive.

q: The plus (+) sign means an ____ in the concentration of the product.
e: Products are formed during a reaction, resulting in a positive change in their concentration.

q: Rate is expressed as a ____ quantity.
e: By convention, reaction rates are always reported as positive values regardless of whether tracking reactants or products.

q: In a general chemical reaction, a, b, c, and d are the stoichiometric ____ of the reactants and products in the balanced chemical equation.
e: Stoichiometric coefficients are necessary to relate the rates of consumption and formation of different species in a reaction.

q: The rate constant, k, explains the relationship between the molar concentration of the reactants and the ____ of a chemical reaction.
e: The rate constant k is the proportionality factor in the rate law equation linking concentration to reaction rate.

q: The mole ratios from the balanced chemical equation can be used to determine the rates of change in ____ of products and reactants.
e: Stoichiometry allows the conversion of the rate of one substance to the rate of another in the same reaction.

q: Magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid giving off ____ gas.
e: The reaction between a reactive metal and an acid typically produces a salt and hydrogen gas.

q: The volume of hydrogen gas released in the process of reaction at time intervals can be ____.
e: Gas syringes or water displacement methods are used to measure the volume of gas evolved over time.

q: The time measurement is expressed in whatever units fit the reaction (seconds, minutes, hours, days, months or ____).
e: The time unit chosen depends on the speed of the reaction, ranging from seconds for fast reactions to years for very slow ones.
